title: Never a sideman; Duke's invitation
summary: He always led his own band; Duke urged him to join him at the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Right. You jammed with a lot of other players and with people in other bands, and things of that nature. But, I don't remember you being a side man with any of the other bands that much. Did you?

man. I always in front of my own band. I used to do guest spots. I did one with Tommy. You know, like he'd be playing somewhere, and this, when he would play, I'd play a number too. It's like I, I think I did one with Goodman once through those years. I did one with Duke. You know, I guess when I was, I had my own band. But, they'd be playing somewhere and I just went and did a number with them. But, I never worked for nobody else. I always had my own band. I know Duke was asking me about it. He wasn't sure I was gonna keep my band when I was in the Savoy. He said 'You don't want those headaches. Come on with me.' You know?
